stem: Which mechanism best explains why C2 deficiency may be associated with autoimmune disease?

options.text: C2 ordinarily helps clear immune complexes and apoptotic debris
C2 is the main immunoglobulin in mucosal secretions
C2 directly generates the neutrophil oxidative burst
C2 is the only complement component involved in MAC formation
C2 primarily increases lymphocyte production in bone marrow

explanation: C2 ordinarily helps clear immune complexes and apoptotic debris, and reduced clearance can contribute to autoimmune disease.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Infectious Disease in Childhood: Global and Regional Perspective

optionExplanations.A: Correct because C2 ordinarily helps clear immune complexes and apoptotic debris, which helps limit autoimmune responses.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because mucosal secretions are dominated by immunoglobulin A, not C2.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the neutrophil oxidative burst is not a function of C2.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because MAC formation involves the terminal complement pathway, not C2 alone.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because C2 does not primarily regulate lymphocyte production in bone marrow.
